questions: At wheel_track 0.09 m, does s-bend max_error fall below 0.0626 m, and does it approach the 0.06 m floor?
Does oval steering_oscillation stay above about 0.25 (it was 0.277 at 0.10 m)? If so, what kp did you use to offset the higher effective yaw gain?
Do the oval and s-bend line_loss_events fall from 2 toward 1, or does the narrower track add line loss?
Does the score exceed 112.54? If not, is the cause the geometry step or the controller setting?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If steering_oscillation is above about 0.25 on the oval, lower kp and report the new value so I can judge whether the geometry is the limit. If s-bend max_error is still above 0.06 m with oscillation below 0.25, propose wheel_track 0.08 m next. If the score falls below 112.54, revert wheel_track to 0.10 m and report the controller settings used.

intent: Narrow wheel_track from 0.10 m to 0.09 m, changing only that parameter relative to iteration 5 (112.54). The five-sensor layout, 12 mm footprints, y = 0.04 m row, wheel radius, body and 0.6 kg mass stay fixed. Expected result: s-bend max_error falls to about 0.061 to 0.062 m, s-bend and oval line-loss events fall from 2 toward 1, and the score rises to about 113 to 120. The Integrator should lower kp if oval steering_oscillation stays above about 0.25 so the yaw response per command stays close to iteration 0. If the score falls below 112.54, revert wheel_track to 0.10 m.
learning: Iteration 5 supports the yaw-authority hypothesis: narrowing the track from 0.12 m to 0.10 m raised the score by 15.7 and improved the oval and s-bend. Iterations 2 and 3 showed that widening the track lowers the score, which is consistent with the contract's yaw relation. Sensor span, footprint size and look-ahead changes (iterations 1 and 3) did not help. Next race, check whether the trend continues at 0.09 m, and whether oscillation and line loss rise enough to offset the gain in yaw authority.
rationale: Iteration 5 (wheel_track 0.10 m, everything else as iteration 4) is the best result so far at 112.54, up from 96.84. The gain came mainly from the oval, where progress rose from 0.43 to 0.55 and the score from 177 to 220. The s-bend improved slightly (max_error 0.0703 to 0.0626 m, score 72 to 77), and the slalom was unchanged. Narrowing the track is therefore moving the platform in the right direction. Two things remain. First, s-bend max_error (0.0626 m) is still above the 0.06 m off-track floor, and line loss is still 2 events per run on the oval and s-bend. Second, oval steering_oscillation rose to 0.277, above the Integrator's 0.25 caution threshold, which points to the higher effective yaw gain from the narrower track. The contract gives turn rate = wheel speed difference / wheel_track, so going from 0.12 m to 0.10 m raised yaw per command by about 20 percent. I will take a smaller step to 0.09 m (about 11 percent more yaw per command), not the 0.08 m the Integrator suggested. This keeps the oscillation increase modest and lets the Integrator restore the yaw response with kp if needed, as they have already planned. Sensors, body, wheel radius and mass stay fixed so that the change isolates turn authority. Expected result: s-bend max_error near 0.061 to 0.062 m, oscillation near 0.25 to 0.28 on the oval (reducible by kp), and a score in the 113 to 120 range. Risk: if oscillation grows enough to cause extra line loss, the score could fall, and I would then revert to 0.10 m.
